bottom_line: In ELITE, losartan versus captopril had the same rate of persisting increases in serum creatinine (10.5% in each group; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%], p=0.63).
implications: These data support that, over 48 weeks in this study population, losartan and captopril had similar rates of confirmed creatinine rise (10.5% in each group; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%], p=0.63). The study also reports lower all-cause mortality with losartan (4.8% vs 8.7%; risk reduction 46% [95% CI 5–69%], p=0.035), fewer discontinuations for adverse effects (12.2% vs 20.8%, p=0.002), and fewer admissions for any reason (22.2% vs 29.7%, p=0.014), while admissions for heart failure were identical (5.7% vs 5.7%).

major_points.text: Double-blind randomised trial in elderly heart-failure patients comparing losartan with captopril for 48 weeks.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 722 ACE inhibitor naive patients ( aged 65 years or more) w ith New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II–IV heart failure and ejection fractions of 40% or less to double-blind losartan (n=352)... or captopril (n=370)... for 48 w eeks.

major_points.text: Persisting increases in serum creatinine occurred equally in both groups (10.5% each).
major_points.quote: There was no significant difference between losartan and captopril in the frequency of the primary endpoint—namely, persisting (confirmed) increases in serum creatinine (10·5% in each group, table 2; risk reduction 2% [95% CI ⫺51% to +36%], p=0·63).

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was lower with losartan than captopril.
major_points.quote: This risk reduction was primarily due to a decrease in all-cause mortality ( 4·8% vs 8·7%; risk reduc t ion 46% [ 95% CI 5–69%], p=0·035).

major_points.text: Fewer patients discontinued assigned therapy for adverse effects with losartan than captopril.

criticisms.text: Observed primary endpoint event rate was lower than assumed, reducing power to detect the planned difference.
criticisms.quote: The event rate proved to be only 10·5% for captopril so the power to detect a 40% reduction was substantially decreased.

criticisms.text: Composite of death and/or admission for heart failure was added as secondary endpoint after completion of patient participation, before unblinding.
criticisms.quote: The composite of death and/or admission for heart failure was added as the secondary endpoint by protocol amendment on completion of patient participation in the study before unblinding.

criticisms.text: Results cannot be extrapolated to younger heart-failure patients or those with diastolic dysfunction.
criticisms.quote: the results cannot be extrapolated to younger heart-failure patients or patients with diastolic dysfunction.

criticisms.text: Women were under-represented and mortality in women requires further study.
criticisms.quote: Only one-third of the patients enrolled in ELITE were women, and mortality in women with heart failure taking losartan or captopril requires further study.

criticisms.text: Cross-study comparisons have limitations and ELITE patients were older.
criticisms.quote: The limitations of cross-study comparisons and the greater age of the patients in this study notwithstanding
